idea.title: Juicero: $699 Wi-Fi juicer pressing subscription produce packs

source.text: Juicero: a $699 Wi-Fi juicer that presses proprietary produce packs sold by subscription at $5 to $8 each, launch country US. Score it as of 2016-03-01: use only evidence published on or before that date (set verdict.as_of). Founder: a funded hardware startup. Just go: do not ask questions. Use the slug juicero.

idea.problem: Fresh cold-pressed juice is expensive ($8-12 a bottle), and juicing at home is messy, slow and needs cleaning.
idea.customer: Affluent, health-conscious urban US households (Bay Area, NYC, LA) who already buy premium cold-pressed juice several times a week.
idea.solution: A $699 Wi-Fi press that squeezes proprietary pre-chopped organic produce packs; the machine scans each pack's code to check freshness before pressing.
claims: packs sold by subscription at $5 to $8 each

context.edge: venture backing and hardware engineering team

assumptions: Pack price $6.50 (midpoint of $5-8); pack yield about 8 oz, not disclosed before 2016-03-01
Customer presses 5 packs a week on average
Channel is direct online sales plus press coverage; no retail deal confirmed before 2016-03-01
Founder is a venture-funded hardware team with the skills to build the press (as stated)
No questions asked: the user said just go

confidence.note: Juicero's own pack yield, pack COGS and retention were not public before 2016-03-01; a teardown or pack cost sheet would raise it.

gross_margin.note: Est. 28% per $6.50 pack after produce, pouch and cold-chain delivery; bottled juice targets ~60%. R5: costs_eat_margin.

ltv_cac.note: Est. LTV $390 vs CAC $200 (CPC / 0.75% conversion): LTV:CAC 1.95, before any hardware subsidy.

pricing_power.note: Anchor is falling: Suja cut 16oz to $7.99 and launched $3.99; Costco sells it at $0.17/oz.

build_effort.note: Custom high-force press plus a produce-pack plant: over 6 months; still unlaunched after raising since 2013.

skills_match.note: Hardware team in place; food safety, fresh-produce sourcing and cold chain are new skills.

capital_needed.note: About $20M raised and ~$120M being raised: fits, but hardware plus a food plant burns capital fast.

time_to_mvp.note: Over 2 years from seed (2013) with no product on sale by early 2016.

sales_cycle.note: $699 considered consumer purchase: days to weeks, not impulse.

channel_readiness.note: Direct online plus tech press exists; CAC for a $699 device unproven (est. $100-$300).

search_demand.note: Juice bars a $2.2B US industry riding the cold-pressed craze; active cleanse culture.

trend.note: Super-premium cold-pressed juice +130.5% YoY (IRI, 52 weeks to 2015-03).

willingness_to_pay.note: Buyers pay up to $10 a 16oz bottle, but leaders are cutting prices to widen the market.

free_alternatives.note: No free equivalent, but $70-$400 juicers and $3.99-$8 bottles do much of the job.

competitor_density.note: Suja ($45M revenue, Coca-Cola $90M stake), Evolution Fresh, Jamba, Pressed Juicery. R5: strong_competitor.

differentiation.note: Only connected juicer found: fresh-pressed at home with no cleanup is a real, specific difference.

legal_regulatory.note: Raw cut-produce plant under new FSMA rules (2015); unpasteurized juice E. coli outbreaks in 2015.

platform_dependency.note: Owns its channel, but each pack needs a server check: Wink hubs bricked by one expired certificate.

market_risk.note: Cold-pressed may be a fad: pioneer chain Organic Avenue shut all 10 stores in 2015-10.

skills.note: Funded hardware team; no pre-2016 evidence of food-manufacturing track record.

assets.note: Kleiner Perkins and Campbell's backing: capital and food-industry network.

interest.note: Founder motivation not documented in pre-2016 sources: scored neutral.

som.reasoning: 5,000 households x ($699 press + 260 packs x $6.50 = $1,690) = $11.9M, ~1.4% of the $844.6M cold-pressed SAM

competitors_found.reasoning: Counted: Suja, Evolution Fresh, BluePrint, Jamba, Pressed Juicery, Juice Press, Costco/retail bottles, Omega, Hurom, Hamilton Beach juicers

price.reasoning: Midpoint of the brief's $5-$8 pack price; no pre-2016 source discloses Juicero pricing

variable_cost_per_unit.reasoning: 8oz pack: ~0.8 lb organic produce at ~$2/lb = $1.75 + pouch and labor $0.75 + cold-chain box ~$11.50 / ~6 packs = $2.00 + spoilage $0.20 = $4.70

gross_margin_pct.reasoning: (6.50 - 4.70) / 6.50 = 27.7%, packs only; press assumed sold near cost

churn_monthly_pct.reasoning: Assumption: no pre-2016 retention benchmark for perishable subscriptions found; 10%/month used

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: US e-commerce averages 3.06% (Monetate 2015); a $699 considered purchase assumed at 0.5-1%, midpoint 0.75%

cac.reasoning: Blended CPC: Facebook $0.31-$0.85, Google $2.32; / 0.5-1% conversion = $31-$464; midpoint ~$200

ltv.reasoning: 5 packs/week x 4.33 = 21.65 packs x $6.50 = $140.7/month x 27.7% margin x 10 months = $390

payback_months.reasoning: CAC $200 / $39 monthly gross profit per subscriber = 5.1 months

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: Assumption: ~50 staff x ~$15k loaded cost + pack facility and leases ~ $1M/month

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: $1,000,000 fixed / $39 gross profit per subscriber per month = 25,641 active subscribers

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: Not on sale as of 2016-03-01 after raising since 2013; at least one quarter to launch and deliver (assumption)

verdict.launch_reason: Founder and investors are in the Bay Area, where premium cold-pressed buyers concentrate.
verdict.cheapest_test: 7-day fake-door in the Bay Area: $699 press pre-order with $50 refundable deposit plus hand-delivered pack trial to 20 households
kill_criteria: Fewer than 300 paid $50 deposits on the Bay Area landing page by day 7 -> stop
Measured cold-chain cost per weekly box above $10 in the day 5 test delivery -> stop
Fewer than 3 packs per week per tester household in the day 1-7 trial -> stop

rescue.change: Drop the press: sell the same organic juice as HPP bottles through grocery retail
rescue.why: Fixes costs_eat_margin (bottled juice ~60% margin) and build_effort; still faces strong_competitor Suja
rescue.requires: Beverage distribution contacts and a brand that beats Suja on shelf

rescue.change: Sell the press to offices, gyms and cafes with daily pack volume
rescue.why: Fixes contribution_margin: one cold-chain drop serves 30+ packs a day instead of 5 a week
rescue.requires: B2B sales and a local delivery route in one metro

rescue.change: Open the system: no pack lock, sell packs as convenience in one metro only
rescue.why: Fixes legal_platform_risk and the Keurig 2.0 graveyard pattern; cuts server dependency
rescue.requires: Accepting lower attach rate on packs

type_checks.note: Est. weekly box: ~$15 (33%) at 7 packs, ~$0 at 3 packs, since cold-chain shipping (~$11.50 a box, gel packs, dim-weight pricing) is fixed per box.
Est. 15% return rate x ~$245 per returned 30 lb press = ~$37 per unit (5% of price); opened packs are a total loss but cheap.

narrative.answer: **NO-GO** at 49. Cold-pressed demand is real and rising, but each $6.50 pack keeps an estimated **28%** margin after cold-chain delivery, and Keurig just showed buyers resist pricey locked-pod machines.
tldr: Demand is real: super-premium cold-pressed juice grew **130.5%** a year (IRI, 2015).
Unit economics fail: est. **28%** pack margin and LTV:CAC 1.95 before any hardware subsidy.
The pod playbook is cracking: Keurig 2.0's DRM cost **23%** of sales; Kold drew price criticism at $369.

key_findings.title: Packs keep an estimated 28% margin
key_findings.detail: At ~10 oz of juice per lb of produce, an 8oz pack costs **$4.70** to make and ship cold, against $6.50; bottled juice targets ~60%.

key_findings.title: Cheaper juice is everywhere and falling
key_findings.detail: Suja cut its 16oz to $7.99 and launched **$3.99** bottles; Costco sells it at $0.17/oz; juicers cost $70-$400.

key_findings.title: Locked-pod machines are stalling
key_findings.detail: Keurig's CEO blamed pod DRM for a **23%** sales drop; its $369 Kold machine drew price criticism in 2015.

narrative.recommendation: Do not build the $699 press as specified. If the team proceeds, test a 7-day Bay Area pre-order and measured cold-chain box cost before tooling.
narrative.steelman: Affluent buyers already pay up to $10 a bottle and cold-pressed grows 75-130% a year; a home press could own a daily habit the way Keurig owned coffee. The evidence: Keurig's own pod model is stalling, and pack margins look thin.

premortem.cause: Packs cost nearly what they sell for once cold-chain delivery is paid, so growth deepens losses.
premortem.early_signal: Cold-chain cost above $10 per weekly box in the first 30 days of deliveries

premortem.cause: Buyers balk at $699 when a $260 juicer or a $3.99 bottle does most of the job.
premortem.early_signal: Under 0.5% of landing-page visitors place a pre-order

premortem.cause: The pack lock and Wi-Fi check trigger Keurig-style backlash or bricked machines.
premortem.early_signal: Over 5% of support tickets about rejected packs or offline machines

changes.what: Super-premium cold-pressed juice grew 130.5% a year in US retail.
Perishable subscriptions scaled: Blue Apron ships 3M meals a month at a $2B valuation.
Connected kitchen appliances went mainstream at CES 2016 (Whirlpool, Samsung, Bosch).
Coca-Cola paid $90M for 30% of Suja, validating the category.

why_now.note: Demand and subscription habits are in place, but Suja moving to $3.99 shows the premium window is narrowing.

icp.who: Affluent, health-focused urban households (Bay Area, NYC, LA) already buying cold-pressed juice several times a week
where: Pressed Juicery and Juice Press stores
icp.pays_for_today: Up to $10 per 16oz bottle (HuffPost, 2014-03); about $65 a day for a delivered cleanse
icp.budget: unknown; a daily habit at $8-$10 implies $2,000-$3,600 a year (estimate)
icp.trigger: Starting a cleanse or a health reset, or tiring of $10 bottles and juicer cleanup

free_alternative.evidence: Searched free and cheap ways to get fresh juice: no free equivalent, but home juicers cost $70-$400 (Tasting Table, 2015-06).

strong_competitor.evidence: Suja: $45M revenue in 2014, $70-80M forecast for 2015, and Coca-Cola paid $90M for 30% in 2015-08.

graveyard.evidence: Keurig 2.0 DRM cut sales 23% (2015-05); Kold at $369 drew price criticism; Quirky went bankrupt (2015-09); Organic Avenue closed (2015-10).

no_distribution.evidence: Direct online and tech press can reach first buyers: est. CAC $200 vs ~$470 first-year gross profit per subscriber.

costs_eat_margin.evidence: Est. $4.70 cost per 8oz pack (produce ~$1.75, cold chain ~$2.00) leaves a 28% gross margin at $6.50.

weak_demand.evidence: Clear: super-premium cold-pressed juice grew 130.5% a year (IRI, 52 weeks to 2015-03-29).

legal_platform_risk.evidence: Raw cut-produce plant under the 2015 FSMA rules; Keurig's pod lock drew antitrust suits (2014-02); Wink's server outage bricked hubs (2015-04).

saturated_wave.evidence: Searched connected juicers 2015-03 to 2016-03: none besides Juicero; about 6 other connected-kitchen launches (June, Teforia, Whirlpool).

customer.pain: $8-$12 bottles add up; home juicing is slow and messy to clean
customer.today: Buy bottles at juice bars or grocery, or run a $260-$400 masticating juicer

use_cases.name: Daily home juice from a $699 press and $6.50 packs
use_cases.effort: Very high: hardware plus a food plant

use_cases.name: Office and gym juice stations with daily packs
use_cases.effort: High: B2B sales and route delivery

scenarios.name: Optimistic
scenarios.note: 30,000 subscribers: barely profitable, ignoring CAC and press subsidy

risks.risk: Pack margin erased by cold-chain delivery
risks.mitigation: Measure box cost in a one-metro pilot before scaling

risks.risk: Pathogen contamination in raw cut-produce packs
risks.mitigation: FSMA preventive controls and lot testing from day one
Keep the QR check for freshness only, allow offline pressing
Position on fresh produce intake, not cleanses

test_plan.step: Launch a Bay Area landing page: $699 pre-order with $50 refundable deposit, $6.50 packs
test_plan.verify: Page live with 1,000 targeted visitors from $300 of Facebook ads

test_plan.step: Hand-deliver 7 prototype packs per week to 20 recruited households
Track pack use per household and ask willingness to pay per pack
test_plan.verify: At least 3 packs used per household per week

test_plan.step: Ship one real cold-chain box by courier and log full cost
Count deposits and compute CAC per deposit
test_plan.verify: 300+ deposits, or CAC per deposit under $100
